key_insight: InterMimicGen turns sparse human-object interaction data into a growing source of robot training experience. By letting robot motion data and a tracking policy co-improve each other, it scales humanoid loco-manipulation beyond static imitation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of using real human-object interaction data for humanoid robots: the data is sparse, diverse, and not directly executable by robots, making it difficult to learn coordinated whole-body locomotion and hand-object manipulation.
method: Consolidate multiple motion-captured human-object interaction datasets into a unified corpus.
Retarget human motions into humanoid robot references while preserving whole-body coordination and dexterous hand-object relations.
Use a self-evolving loop where robot-generated motion data improves the tracking policy, and the stronger policy generates better robot motion data.
impact: This matters because it provides a scalable way to build humanoid imitation learning systems from messy real-world interaction data. For practitioners, it suggests a path toward more robust loco-manipulation policies without relying solely on expensive robot demonstrations.

paper_title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
paper_authors: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi
